source.title: Scaling Down Deep Learning with MNIST-1D

record.tranche_reason: Reports results on label noise in the new MNIST-1D setting, bearing on V4.
record.gate_note: The paper tests only 15% label noise against no label noise. It does not report a sweep from no corruption to fully random labels. Rows record the described test-error behavior at the interpolation threshold; precise values are shown only in Figure 5.
record.test_reason: The study demonstrates fitting partially corrupted labels and spatially shuffled inputs in the new MNIST-1D setting, bearing on V4 and V3 respectively.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the double-descent result, but omits that increasing capacity beyond interpolation reduces test error again. It also omits the relevant shuffled-input result: MLP, CNN, and GRU fit the training data perfectly, while shuffling substantially reduces CNN and GRU test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses MNIST-1D and varies model size under a single label-noise level; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Label noise condition (none versus 15%); model size is swept.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error peaks near interpolation and then falls as model size increases under 15% label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partially corrupted MNIST-1D labels produce model-size double descent in MLP and CNN classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 235, 2024
record.problems: The label-noise experiment tests only 15% corruption. The precise plotted error values are not stated in the text, and the CNN result is described only qualitatively.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, chance test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence changes across corruption fractions.
Independently permuted inputs and pure Gaussian-noise inputs. Adding Gaussian noise to structured digit templates does not test fitting pure noise.
A corruption sweep toward fully random labels, steady test-error degradation toward chance, and perfect training fit throughout that sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their removal on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.

missing.what: Separate shuffled-input fitting rows for MLP, CNN, and GRU: each achieves 100% training accuracy. Their shuffled-input test accuracies are 68 ± 2%, 56 ± 2%, and 57 ± 2%, respectively. This is a shared feature permutation that removes local spatial structure.
missing.locator: Table 1; Section 4, Shuffling sanity check; Figure 2

record.verdict_notes: The original limits_scope verdict confuses untested parts with contrary evidence. A model-size test-error peak does not challenge smooth degradation across label-noise fractions. Neither original claim source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling of the training set and the claimed training and test errors.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper compares no label noise with 15% label noise only; it does not test a gradual sweep toward all labels corrupted or report test error approaching chance.
Regularization effects on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: MLP classifier
rows.size_stated: one hidden layer; around 50 neurons at the interpolation threshold
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST-1D with 15% label noise while varying hidden-layer size.
rows.measure: Test error at the interpolation threshold, where training error reaches zero
rows.baseline: No label noise: test error did not peak.
rows.value: Test error peaked at the interpolation threshold, at around 50 neurons in the hidden layer; precise value figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the peak and zero training error at the threshold; it gives no precise test-error value.
rows.check: Zero training error with 15% label noise supports the fitting component of V4. The test-error peak is measured across model sizes, not corruption fractions, so it does not establish or contradict smooth degradation as corruption increases. Incomplete coverage of V4 does not make the observed fitting effect partial.

rows.subject: CNN classifier with three convolutional layers
rows.size_stated: three convolutional layers; number of channels varied
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST-1D with 15% label noise while varying number of channels.
rows.measure: Test error behavior with training error shown in Figure 5
rows.baseline: No label noise comparison is shown for the MLP, not this CNN.
rows.value: Qualitatively similar behavior using the CNN architecture; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The text does not specify the CNN's exact peak location or test-error value.
rows.check: Section 5.2 describes qualitatively similar CNN interpolation behavior with 15% label noise. This supports fitting at that noise level; it does not measure a corruption-fraction trajectory. Exact CNN errors and the interpolation location cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

relationships.condition: MNIST-1D with 15% label noise and sufficient model capacity
relationships.reason: R1 reports zero training error at roughly 50 hidden neurons; R2 reports qualitatively similar CNN interpolation behavior. These support fitting partially corrupted labels.
relationships.display_finding: Training error reached zero at roughly 50 hidden neurons, with qualitatively similar perfect fitting in CNNs.

tranche.reason: MNIST-1D provides a new setting with results on fitting partially corrupted labels and spatially shuffled inputs.

source_check.notes: V4 evidence concerns fitting at 15% label noise while varying capacity, not a corruption-fraction trajectory. V3 evidence concerns shared feature shuffling; independent permutations and Gaussian replacement are untested here.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The MLP result shows a test-error peak at the zero-training-error threshold, but the study tests only one nonzero noise fraction and does not establish steady degradation toward chance (R1); the CNN result is described only as qualitatively similar (R2).
